This is from my own experience with these older abandoned computers. Micro$oft and the motherboard/computer manufacturers have conspired to lobotomize the BIOS so that any upgrades are nigh impossible. I have a Dell netbook with .5GB RAM and that is all it will accept. I have a HP Compaq which will only accept 1 GB. I have attempted installing 64-bit Linux on some of these computers and had major problems so all I could install was 32-bit Linux: I am looking at you HP a1245c originally installed with 32-bit Windows XP Media Center. The motherboard BIOS will only accept a max of 3 GB.

So be aware that some later distros of Linux may have problems with installation and running.

TL;DR: This is done to cut hardware costs

In laymans terms, the number of pins on your CPU and northbridge (a chip on your motherboard used for numerous critical functions) is what limits the RAM and more pins = more money. A 32-bit operating system can't support more than 3GB anyways so the engineers saw it as a waste of money to put more pins on the northbridge. The creators of many laptops also probably figured most people won't ever need more than 8 GB of RAM so to cut costs they used fewer pins. Higher end laptops will put higher limits to allow for more upgrading.
